AUTHOR: P. Mukherjee
TITLE: UWOT-Net: Underwater Object Tracking by Attention Driven Network in Unconstrained Marine Environments
SPECIES: BrackishMOT classes: fish, tiny fish, crab, prawn, starfish, jellyfish; GMOT40 fish category; UTB180 underwater objects
DATA: BrackishMOT (98 sequences), GMOT-40 (fish category, 4 videos), UTB180 (180 web videos)
V_EV: Sec III-B: 'for the GMOT40 and UTB180 datasets, the original image is fed directly to the encoder since these datasets are not degraded by turbidity and backlight scattering.'
D2: BrackishMOT: 78 training / 20 test sequences; GMOT40: 3 train / 1 test fish video; UTB180: 130 train / 50 test sequences
D_EV: Sec IV-B: 'Our model underwent training on 78 sequences and was then assessed on 20 additional sequences dedicated to testing its performance.'
R_EV: Sec IV-B: model trained and tested separately within each dataset (BrackishMOT, GMOT40, UTB180); no cross-dataset evaluation.
C_EV: Sec IV-C: 'the newly proposed model has notably diminished the frequency of ID switches across all the datasets (See Tables: I, II, V)'
E_EV: Tables I-V report only HOTA, MOTA, MOTP, MT/PT/ML and ID counts.
ARCH: UWOT-Net: RAUNE-Net enhancement + ResNet-50 + deformable-DETR encoder-decoder tracking-by-attention (TrackFormer/TrTr-style)
METR: HOTA, MOTA, MOTP, MT, PT, ML, IDs
NOTE: Included on the basis of BrackishMOT (allowed monitoring dataset); GMOT40 and UTB180 (web videos) are benchmark collections. Platform/region not described in the paper (PLAT=NR). BrackishMOT split by sequence (78/20) - unclear whether this is the dataset's predefined split; coded 영상(video). Brackish and GMOT40 models trained from scratch; UTB180 fine-tuned from CrowdHuman/MOT17 and COCO DETR weights. BrackishMOT results are pooled across 6 classes, not fish-only. C5 coded because ID switches are measured; no score threshold reported.
